claims: Boeing builds the core stage of the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Northrop Grumman provides the solid rocket boosters for the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Aerojet Rocketdyne (an L3Harris company) produces the RS-25 engines for the Artemis program’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Lockheed Martin builds the Orion spacecraft.
Boeing produces the 212-foot core stage for the Artemis missions, which houses the main engines and flight systems.
Northrop Grumman manufactures the twin five-segment solid rocket boosters for the Artemis missions, which provide 75% of the thrust at launch.
Aerojet Rocketdyne supplies the RS-25 engines and other propulsion systems for the Artemis missions.
Airbus builds the European Service Module (ESM) for the Orion capsule for the European Space Agency.
United Launch Alliance (ULA) developed the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
The Artemis II crew's journey in space has begun.
The SLS is managed by NASA.
Different components of the SLS are manufactured across the U.S. and in Europe.
